root_cause.text: `sched_mm_cid_fork()` accounted a new `task_struct` as an MMCID user too early in `fork()`—before the task was linked into the thread list and global task list—so concurrent forks could trigger `mm_cid_fixup_tasks_to_cpus()` and miss that just-forked task, leaving its allocated CID unfixed and causing stalls.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says “A newly forked task is accounted as MMCID user before the task is visible in the process' thread list and the global task list,” and the patch moves `sched_mm_cid_fork()` from `copy_mm()` to `sched_post_fork()` “after the new task becomes visible in the thread and the task list”; it also updates `mm_cid_do_fixup_tasks_to_cpus()` comments to note the incoming task is “already visible,” confirming the bug was the visibility/accounting ordering in the sched/mmcid fork path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused `sched_mm_cid_fork()` declaration from the CONFIG_SCHED_MM_CID header interface.
intent_record.what: A single function declaration, `void sched_mm_cid_fork(struct task_struct *t);`, was removed from the `#ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_MM_CID` section of the header.
intent_record.how: This changes the available interface by no longer exposing the `sched_mm_cid_fork()` prototype to code including this header, which means callers can no longer rely on this declaration from this location.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused no-op `sched_mm_cid_fork()` stub from the non-enabled code path.
intent_record.what: The inline no-op definition of `sched_mm_cid_fork(struct task_struct *t)` was removed from the `#else` branch, while the other inline stubs in that block were left unchanged.
intent_record.how: When the relevant configuration is disabled, this specific helper is no longer available as an empty inline function from this section, so any callers must rely on a declaration from elsewhere or no longer call it in this configuration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the `sched_mm_cid_fork()` call from `copy_mm()` so MM CID fork handling is no longer performed there.
intent_record.what: The call to `sched_mm_cid_fork(tsk);` was removed from `copy_mm(u64 clone_flags, struct task_struct *tsk)` after assigning `tsk->mm` and `tsk->active_mm`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, `copy_mm()` no longer performs the scheduler MM CID fork handling for the task during mm setup, so that associated setup side effect will not occur at this point in task cloning.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unnecessary MM CID exit call from the fork failure cleanup path.
intent_record.what: In the `bad_fork_cleanup_mm` error path of `copy_process()`, the call to `sched_mm_cid_exit(p)` was removed from the `if (p->mm)` cleanup block, leaving only `mm_clear_owner(p->mm, p);` and `mmput(p->mm);`.
intent_record.how: If process creation fails after an `mm` has been assigned, the cleanup path no longer performs the `sched_mm_cid_exit()` operation for that task. This changes the fork error cleanup sequence by skipping that scheduler/MM CID teardown step before releasing the memory context.

intent_record.intent_summary: Invoke mm CID fork setup from `sched_post_fork()` so forked tasks receive the required mm CID initialization.
intent_record.what: A forward declaration for `static void sched_mm_cid_fork(struct task_struct *t);` was added above `sched_post_fork()`, and `sched_post_fork()` was modified to call `sched_mm_cid_fork(p)` before calling `uclamp_post_fork(p)` and `scx_post_fork(p)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, every task entering `sched_post_fork()` will now also run the mm CID fork handling path, ensuring the task's mm-related CID state is initialized or propagated during fork processing before the later scheduler-specific post-fork hooks run.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix mm_cid task accounting during CPU fixup by correcting the users count calculation and ensuring the remaining task is still processed.
intent_record.what: The code in `mm_cid_do_fixup_tasks_to_cpus()` changes the users accounting calculation from `mm->mm_cid.users - 2` to `mm->mm_cid.users - 1`, and removes the early `if (!users) return;` exit. The surrounding comment was also rewritten to explain that the caller is already removed from the users count, while the incoming task is visible and still needs to be counted.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the fixup logic now accounts for one fewer subtraction in the users count, so the function no longer incorrectly skips processing when only one user remains. This allows the active task and any eligible threads to be properly considered during the mm_cid task-to-CPU fixup, preventing accounting from being prematurely treated as empty.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid dereferencing or warning on a missing `mm` in `sched_mm_cid_fork` by returning early and keeping the CID state check separate.
intent_record.what: The function `sched_mm_cid_fork(struct task_struct *t)` was changed from non-static to `static`, and its initial check was split: it now immediately returns if `t->mm` is NULL, then separately issues `WARN_ON_ONCE(t->mm_cid.cid != MM_CID_UNSET)` instead of warning on both conditions together.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function will no longer emit a warning or continue when called for a task without an `mm`; it simply exits early in that case. For tasks with an `mm`, it still warns if the CID is unexpectedly already set, preserving the sanity check while avoiding an invalid dereference of `mm`-related state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a no-op fallback for `sched_mm_cid_fork()` when `CONFIG_SCHED_MM_CID` is disabled.
intent_record.what: A new empty static inline stub for `sched_mm_cid_fork(struct task_struct *t)` was added inside the `#else /* CONFIG_SCHED_MM_CID */` block, alongside the existing no-op `mm_update_cpus_allowed()` stub.
intent_record.how: When `CONFIG_SCHED_MM_CID` is disabled, code can now call `sched_mm_cid_fork()` without causing an undefined reference or requiring additional conditional compilation; at runtime it performs no action in that configuration.

Remove the unused no-op `sched_mm_cid_fork()` stub from the non-enabled code path.

Remove the unnecessary MM CID exit call from the fork failure cleanup path.

consistency_review.core_intent: Move mm CID fork initialization out of copy_mm() and into sched_post_fork() so forked tasks get the required mm CID setup.

relevance_review.reason: The change only removes an unused function declaration from a header interface. It does not modify fork-time MMCID accounting, task list linkage timing, or the fixup logic involved in the race described by the vulnerability root cause.

The change only removes an unused no-op stub in the disabled code path. It does not address the race in `sched_mm_cid_fork()` where a task was counted as an MMCID user too early during fork, which is the root cause of the vulnerability.

The root cause is that the task was counted as an MMCID user too early during fork, before being linked into task lists. This change moves MMCID fork initialization out of copy_mm() and into sched_post_fork(), which directly fixes that ordering issue.

This change only removes an MM CID exit call from fork failure cleanup. The root cause is about accounting the new task as an MMCID user too early during successful fork setup, before it is linked into task lists, which can race with fixup and leave a CID unfixed. The described change does not address that timing/race issue.

The change directly targets mm_cid task accounting during CPU fixup, which is part of the same root-cause area. Correcting the users count and ensuring the remaining task is processed addresses the race/missed-task behavior that could leave a CID unfixed and cause stalls.

The change only adds an early return when mm is missing and separates a CID state check. It does not address the root cause of accounting a forked task too early before list linkage, nor the concurrent miss in mm_cid_fixup_tasks_to_cpus().

The change only adds a no-op fallback when CONFIG_SCHED_MM_CID is disabled. It does not address the fork-time accounting order bug where a task was marked as an MMCID user too early and missed by mm_cid_fixup_tasks_to_cpus().

candidates.rationale: This line accounts the new task as an MMCID user during copy_mm(), which is too early because the task is not yet linked into the thread list or global task list. That premature accounting is the root cause of concurrent fixup missing the forked task.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement prematurely accounts the newly forked task as an MMCID user during copy_mm(), before it is linked into the thread list and global task list. That early accounting allows concurrent mm_cid_fixup_tasks_to_cpus() to miss the task, leaving its CID unfixed and causing stalls.

The root cause says `sched_mm_cid_fork()` accounted the new `task_struct` as an MMCID user too early in `fork()` before it was linked into the thread/task lists, allowing concurrent `mm_cid_fixup_tasks_to_cpus()` to miss it. This code calls `sched_mm_cid_fork(tsk)` immediately after assigning `mm`/`active_mm`, with no indication of list linkage or any deferred accounting, so the vulnerable construct is present. There is also no fix visible here (no delayed call, no additional synchronization, and no check preventing early enrollment), so `is_fixed` is false.
